recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core source edit is needed for FHIR-12968 unless a future work-group decision separately revisits the broader Definition/Canonical wording.
issue_request: FHIR-12968 was a Published/Persuasive non-substantive technical correction for the FHIR-core Definition pattern. It asked whether Definition.useContext should avoid the spelling "usageContexts" and asked to remove Definition.purpose prose that referred to nonexistent "comments" and "relatedArtifacts" elements; the Jira comment accepted only the common-source cleanup for purpose and said the plural use-context wording was not itself a problem.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit ee7516b200ca78d9a8926d6ae0827f9c6d3c9364, "Fix typos", which did not cite the Jira key but was authored by Lloyd McKenzie on 2017-03-20 immediately after his Jira comment and removed the stale "comments element, or relatedArtifacts" wording from source/definition/definition-spreadsheet.xml. No separate application commit for changing Definition.useContext was found, matching the Jira comment that disagreed with that requested change.
additional_context: Definition is an active logical pattern in source/fhir.ini, so source/definition/definition-spreadsheet.xml is in current build scope. Later Published issue FHIR-40406 aligned Definition with Canonical in commit 1e7ed5c7a6146f8bd69ebfb2169cd9c687d9e34d, changing the current Definition.useContext comment to "useContexts" and refining the Definition.purpose wording without reintroducing the stale references. No relevant Zulip or Confluence record was found that conflicts with the Jira/source history.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source no longer contains the disputed "comments element, or relatedArtifacts" text, and the current use-context wording is clear and consistent with the later Definition alignment work.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Definition/Canonical alignment changed the same Definition.useContext and Definition.purpose source and confirms the current wording is intentional.
